The versions release-please owns, and the only version-bearing file in this repository. Keys are release-please component names, which are the deployable names — `identity`, `identity-admin`, `identity-jobs` — deliberately identical to the wrangler worker names, the moon project aliases, the git tag prefixes and the Cloudflare Version tags, so that a tag, a version id and a worker name can be compared by eye (ADR-0012 §7, `docs/operations/deployment-model.md`).

`0.0.0` for all three, and that is the true state rather than a placeholder: NO TAG EXISTS, no version has ever been uploaded to any environment, and nothing has been deployed. A repository that has cut no release carries a manifest of zeros, and a manifest of zeros is honest in a way that `0.1.0` is not — a `0.1.0` here would claim a first release that was never cut.

Only the three deployables appear. The nine internal crates and the two frontends are absent by design (ADR-0012 step 7, ADR-0015 step 1): the crates are not production release units and are never tagged, and a frontend is a release COMPONENT of its Worker rather than a component of its own — there is no `identity-web` tag and there never will be one.

This file is bumped by release-please and reviewed in its release PR. It is not read by any build, and `pnpm arch` reads `release-please-config.json` rather than this one.
